summary: Documented step M1-S03 (tested -> documented) in build tier2-webhook: re-rendered PLAN.md, appended 9 decisions to decisions.md (the round-1 template-closure refusal and remedy B; the S2-F-04 getSalesforceBaseUrl/version-gate lesson; the S2-F-05 LongTextArea-filter fault; the P1 missing trigger kill switch; the UNVERIFIED Severity mapping; the TestDataFactory duplication for M1-S05; the setMock-ordering library contradiction; and a newly-discovered no-op prose-only amendment that left the manual test's stale HttpClient.cls clause unchanged), and updated traceability.md: 7 existing rows (REQ-001, REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-005, REQ-006, REQ-008, REQ-009) updated in place with M1-S03 artefacts and narration, 6 new rows minted (REQ-011 through REQ-016) for M1-S03 inputs no earlier row covered. scale: feature keeps the workbook optional and skipped, unchanged from every prior pass. check_rtm.py now reports 0 coverage gaps and 0 orphans (was 11 orphans before this pass).
confidence_rationale: Every artefact this step produced now has a traceability row, every new row carries a real source_req_id (minted this pass, anchored) and a verification note, and re-running the RTM checker shows 0 orphans and 0 coverage gaps with no duplicates. Held to MEDIUM rather than HIGH because the workbook step type this build uses (scale: feature) is documented via traceability.md rather than the ten-section workbook, several rows' evidence rests on source inspection and static checkers rather than an executed Apex test (no compile check exists in this design-only build until a human runs mock_deploy.py), and this pass surfaced a new, unresolved plan-hygiene defect (D-M1S03-08) rather than only recording pre-identified ones.

process_observations.observation: Every one of the 11 orphan Apex artefacts check_rtm.py flagged before this pass now resolves to a traceability row after this pass's updates, with 0 coverage gaps and 0 warnings on re-run.

Two run-3 source fixes (S2-F-04, S2-F-05) that the org caught and the operator recorded in deploy-order.md were independently re-confirmed present in the shipped .cls files by this pass's own grep, not merely trusted from the artefact's prose.

The amendment plan.json records at steps[M1-S03].amendments[2] (prose_only: true, reason: re-word the stale HttpClient.cls manual-test clause) wrote no actual change: the current acceptance_tests field is byte-identical to the amendment's own 'before' snapshot, so the M1 gate's manual test still names a template this build does not ship.

artefacts/M1-S03/deploy-order.md section 6 states 'all six production classes are with sharing' and 'both SOQL statements carry WITH USER_MODE', but a grep this pass over the shipped .cls files counts five with-sharing classes and three WITH USER_MODE SOQL statements -- the compliance claim holds, the artefact's own arithmetic is off by one in each count.

M1-S03 ships CaseTrigger.trigger as an after-update trigger on Case, and none of this build's 45 clarifications say whether the target org already has an after-update trigger on Case; a pre-existing trigger of the same name would collide at deploy, which only a human checking the target org can resolve.

Now that M1-S03 is documented, milestone-verifier should run once M1-S04 and M1-S05 are also documented, since all three of D-M1S03-04 (missing kill switch), D-M1S03-08 (the no-op prose amendment) and D-M1S04-03 (unproven scheduling-user access) are open M1-gate confirmation items this build has accumulated across steps.
process_observations.followup_reason: It is the agent that runs cross-step checks and produces the acceptance report the M1 gate actually reads, and it can roll all of this pass's open items into one report rather than leaving them scattered across three steps' documentation.
